title: Beyond Metrics: Evaluating LLMs Effectiveness in Culturally Nuanced, Low-Resource Real-World Scenarios

live_model.evidence: Sec 3.1: "We evaluated three OpenAI models: GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4-32k..., and GPT-3.5-Turbo"; Figure 1 F1-score chart, one of seven compared models.

prompt.location: Figure 3 ("the standardized prompt that we used for evaluating all seven LLMs")
prompt.note: Single fixed sentiment-classification prompt shared by all 7 models.

claim.metric: weighted F1 score (%), sentiment classification, WhatsApp chat dataset
claim.location: Figure 1 ("Overall F1 score comparison of the models"); GPT-4-Turbo bar shown between GPT-3.5-Turbo and Mixtral-8x7b, but no exact value is printed as text or in a table

data.source: Private WhatsApp chat dataset (Karusala et al. 2021 / Mondal et al. 2021) of HIV-support-group messages in Nairobi; paper states "the dataset is not publicly available, but researchers can request access by contacting the authors"

notes: GPT-4-Turbo is genuinely run live as one of 7 evaluated models with a standardized zero-shot prompt (Figure 3) over a fixed 3,719-message set, and its per-sentiment performance is discussed at length, but only via bar-chart figures (1, 2, 4) -- no exact numeric value for GPT-4-Turbo is printed in text or a table. More fundamentally, the WhatsApp dataset (real, sensitive health-related messages) is explicitly not public and is gated behind author request, blocking reproduction independent of the number issue.
